London, 6<sup>th</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Xstrata** might be willing to sell its 25%stake in Lonmin Platinum as the group might see less potential for integration with its own operations, Paul Cliff, an analyst with Nomura Securities, said.  Cliff said: “Clearly, Xstrata is not a distressed seller and would only entertain attractive offers with a substantial premium. We think there may be some interest from gold producers looking to diversify into platinum while the gold price remains strong.”   Xstrata’s stake in Lonmin was worth £611 million (R8.3 billion) at Friday’s close. An Xstrata spokeswoman declined to comment on the report.  A sale of the Lonmin stake would, however, appear to be a change in strategy for Xstrata. A buyout of Lonmin is considered vital to Xstrata achieving its output goal of 1 million ounces of platinum a year by 2018, announced last March.   Cliff said Xstrata was likely to embark on acquisitions over the medium term, but scope to fund any acquisitions through either debt or equity was “very limited” in the short term. _Source:  Business Report_ 

**Platmin** has resumed mining operations at its Pilanesberg project following a safety-related suspension late last month held after the death of a worker.   The Pilanesberg mine is expected to reach steady state production of 250koz/y of PGMs and gold by Q3 09. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Ridge Mining** announced that the Blue Ridge Mine has today delivered its first concentrate to Impala Refining Services. The mine is due to reach its full capacity of 125,000 4E ounces of PGMs/year in concentrate during Q3 09. _Source: Ridge Mining_ 

**Some General Motors bondholders** and the largest U.S. auto union are betting the new president may now be using bankruptcy as a stick to get all parties to reach a deal. In setting a two-month deadline for GM and a one-month deadline for Chrysler, the calculation from bondholders and the UAW is that Obama is trying to force their hand and reach an agreement.  The thinking is that President Obama will be reluctant to put the fate of automakers and unionized workers in the hands of a bankruptcy judge. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**GM** said about 600 hourly workers who tentatively accepted a special attrition retirement or buy-out package last month have changed their minds.   About 7,600 workers initially accepted the offers. Many had until March 31 to reconsider; most of the remaining 7,000 workers left the company by April 1. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Large TFT LCD producers** in Korea plan to increase shipments 23 %  this year while producers in Taiwan plan to increase shipments only 12 %, according to a DisplaySearch report. Taiwan producers, however, plan a surge of output in 2H 09, according to the Quarterly Large-Area Production Strategy Report from DisplaySearch.   Large panel producers in Korea grew their output 23 % in 2008 and plan to repeat the growth this year by bringing new TFT fabrica

tion plants on-line and supporting affiliated brands such as LG and Samsung. From the first half to the second half of 2009, Korea producers plan to allocate 25 % more glass substrate area and fabricate 27 % more panels. This plan calls for a 2 % reduction in the average glass area per panel in 2H 09, as Korea producers concentrate on increasing their output for notebook PC applications more than their output for monitor or TV applications, and average size of notebook panels decreases.   The average large panel is consuming less glass substrate area as producers adjust their product mix in response to consumer preference.   The average glass substrate area allocated per panel increased 2 % in 08; producers indicate it will decrease 2 % in 2009. _Source:  EE Times Asia_
